mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in periods where UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces revenue expectations for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of months where INDPRO falls by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure, which increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous year's maximum for three consecutive months signals a housing market boom, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous year max for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of sustained above-peak housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months is a contradictory signal indicating labor market churning; this uncertainty depresses investor confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise over two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 10-year average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 10-year average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower when RSAFS exceeds its 10-year average for six consecutive months.
